$comment: Schemas that tools/*.py declares and src/*.rs deliberately does not. This is the one hand-authored file in the index, so bbindex.py resolves every entry against the tree on each run: an entry no tool declares any more fails as stale, and an entry marked must_not_exist_in_rust fails if it ever appears in src/. Without that second check the allowlist would quietly absorb the loss of the very independence it records. Anything a tool declares that is not listed here fails the schema gate -- that is how a rename landing in one language and not the other gets caught.

local.why: The definition-tag domain for the metric registry. The registry is generated from Markdown by Python and consumed as docs/metrics/registry.tsv; the Rust crate never hashes a metric definition, so there is nothing for it to declare.

A negative control, held in MUTATED_SCHEMA. The vector suite re-encodes an observation under a schema the decoder must reject, proving the schema tag is inside the hashed domain rather than decoration. If this ever appears in src/ the control has stopped being wrong and stops testing anything.
A synthetic parent digest that roots the vector chain, so the fixtures do not depend on a real prior receipt. It is test scaffolding, not a protocol object.

The independent renderer oracle. PROTOCOL.md's semantic-renderer level requires an independent specification to agree at every pixel, and re-running the same implementation is not independent verification. A Rust declaration of this schema would mean the oracle had been folded into the implementation it is supposed to check.
The oracle's depth buffer, independent for the same reason as the renderer profile above.
